findings.title: A search using an unrecognised note property silently returns every note in the tree, including root and _hidden
findings.priorityNote: Strongest: silent whole-tree results from a one-letter typo, the manual's own example is the typo, unreported, and the fix is two lines.

findings.title: A search whose text starts with '#' never loads note sizes from the database, so identical queries answer differently depending on search history; note.revisionCount is always 0
findings.priorityNote: Second: order-dependent search results (the same query answers differently depending on what was searched before it) plus a second, unconditionally dead property; the corrected mechanism is unreported and is worse than the original claim.

findings.title: The "Search now" button on a saved search creates a new empty search note instead of running the saved search
findings.priorityNote: Third: a visible, one-click-reproducible UI bug where the only control offered for running a saved search runs a different search; unreported and independent of the feature request that partially overlaps it.

findings.title: The search lexer strips commas even inside quotes, so no comma-bearing label value (including #geolocation) can be matched by equality
findings.priorityNote: Fourth: the manual instructs users to author exactly the value that cannot be searched, unreported, with a one-line cause and an undocumented escape hatch.

findings.title: POST /api/notes/<parent>/children without a content key returns 500 for every note type, while a missing title is silently defaulted
findings.priorityNote: Fifth: an unreported API robustness defect, broader than originally recorded (every note type, not just book), with a one-line fix and an internal inconsistency that argues it.

findings.title: PUT /api/notes/<noteId>/clone-to-branch/<branchId> with no request body returns 500 and leaks a minified variable name to the caller
findings.priorityNote: Sixth: same family as F12 and equally cheap to fix, ranked lower only because it also leaks a minified variable name and the repo has already declined a same-class report once.

findings.title: Note titles are never HTML-sanitised on the create or rename path, contradicting the manual's statement that HTML in a title is stripped for security
findings.priorityNote: Seventh: a documented security promise the code does not keep, but no exploitable render path was found, so it files as a correctness and defence-in-depth issue rather than an advisory.

findings.title: The fuzzy operators ~= and ~* never lex, so a fuzzy query silently degrades to a label-existence or match-everything query
findings.priorityNote: Eighth: already reported and already fixed in an open PR, so the value left is a PR comment confirming it on the current release and correcting the stale symptom on the tracking issue.

findings.title: A multi-word = query in quick search is a substring compare, so a longer title matches what the manual calls an exact match
findings.priorityNote: Last: accurately reported already and fixed by a mergeable open PR, so there is nothing left to file.
